rationale: Two independent controlled studies converge in an easing direction for oral pumpkin seed oil on depressive symptoms: a 12-week double-blind randomized human trial in 35 postmenopausal women (31 analyzed; Gossell-Williams 2011, PMID21545273) reported median depression item staying at 0 (IQR 0-1) on 2 g/day Cucurbita pepo seed oil versus rising from 0 to 1 (IQR 0-2) on wheat germ oil (unadjusted endpoint p=.046 across 18 exploratory items), and a six-week chronic mild stress rat experiment (DOI10.21608/ejchem.2024.310875.10173, grouped with the related 2022 cortical report as one program) reported higher sucrose preference and shorter tail-suspension immobility with oral pumpkin seed oil versus stressed controls. Active wheat-germ-oil comparator, floor effect, unverified cold-press extraction, exploratory single-item rating, and absence of a Parkinson cohort keep the easing lean at minimal_signal. The distinct 2017 study verifies a cold-pressed oil and gives unchanged depression counts within the oil group at 12 weeks. The seed comparator figure has an unexplained denominator and gives no item-level treatment effect. This tempers the indirect supportive evidence without establishing a direction for Parkinson depression.

A Parkinson self-experiment included ground white mustard in broccoli tea and described balance, with no recorded fall count or mustard-only comparison. Black mustard extract changed animal motor tests without a clinical fall-frequency measure. The bibliographic lead resolves to a historical whole-seed pamphlet and its review without a fall measure. A verified 2018 external seed acupressure trial shows inconclusive mobility, balance and fear-of-falling group comparisons. Neither supplies an oral ground-seed fall-count estimate.

The animal work measures corrective stepping or other motor proxies after juice or extract. A healthy-volunteer cranberry-juice registration gives no posted result or explicit bradykinesia measure. The cooked cranberry claim remains unresolved. The resveratrol review lists European cranberry without a cooked fruit assignment or bradykinesia comparison. The original aged-rat study reports a favorable inclined-screen latency result and no accelerating-rotarod diet comparison effect. These measure balance and strength or coordination and do not supply a bradykinesia contrast.
